subject: treasureChest
pitch: A pirate's treasure chest with its lid thrown open. Weathered dark wood planks bound with rusty iron straps and studs, a heavy padlock hanging loose, and spilling out of it: gold coins, a pearl necklace, a jewelled goblet and a few red and green gems. A small skull-and-crossbones is carved on the front.
reasoning:
I'm planning out a treasure chest model with an open lid, wooden planks, iron straps, studs, a padlock, scattered coins, a pearl necklace, a goblet, gems, and a carved skull-and-crossbones design, aiming for realistic proportions around 0.9m wide. I'm starting with a seeded random number generator and setting up the materials needed.

Now I'm detailing textures and colors for the wood, iron, gold, pearl, ruby, emerald, and bone elements, including a plaque approach for the carved skull on the front panel. I'm designing the chest body as offset plank boxes, adding iron straps and corner brackets with rows of studs, and building the lid as a hinged, curved half-cylinder shape that rotates open at the back.

Working out the half-cylinder rotation and positioning math so the lid's flat edge aligns correctly with the hinge line at the back top of the chest...

So I need to shift the geometry so the back edge sits at z=0 for the pivot, then rotate about X by roughly -110° to swing the front edge up and backward into an open position. For the interior, I'm adding a dark recessed surface near the top plus a scattering of coin-like thin cylinders piled inside.

For the coins I'll use instanced meshes to keep performance reasonable, mounding them inside the chest with some spilling over the front rim onto the floor. I'm also planning a lathe-geometry goblet, gem shapes nestled among the coins, a pearl necklace draped across the pile, and a hanging padlock attached to a front hasp with a shackle and body box.

For the decoration I'm placing a skull-and-crossbones plaque on the front face using a canvas texture, and generating wood-grain textures via canvas drawing to apply as material maps on the plank boxes that make up the chest body.

Adding iron hardware...

Still writing lid geometry...

Now I'm thinking through the chest body itself—making it hollow rather than solid so coins can visibly pile at the open top, with a dark interior floor visible when the lid is raised, rather than a solid box that would look wrong with coins spilling over it.

For the interior, I'll add a slightly raised dark "well" plane inset within a thin wooden rim frame around the top edge, giving the coins something to rest on that looks like the inside of the chest.

For the coins themselves, I'm planning an instanced mesh of roughly 220 gold cylinders arranged in a mound shape using randomized positions and heights based on distance from center, plus a smaller scattering of spilled coins on the floor in front, each with slight random tilt for natural variation.

Now I'm adding decorative treasure details: a draped necklace made from pearl instances placed along a curved path over the pile, and a jeweled goblet built from a lathe-generated shape with a torus rim and gem accent, positioned so its base sits roughly at the pile's surface height even if it slightly overlaps the coins.

I'm scattering gem shapes (octahedron forms for rubies and emeralds with subtle emissive glow) across the pile and floor, plus a skull-and-crossbones textured plaque on the chest's front face, and working out placement for an iron hasp plate and a padlock hanging loosely from it near the top-right of the front panel.

Now I'm positioning the padlock's body and shackle geometry relative to the hasp loop, then laying out the chest's strap bands — adjusting the hasp and skull plaque positions slightly so the vertical straps don't collide with them.

I'm working out the strap wrapping around the body as boxes across front, sides, and back, plus stud spheres along the bands, corner brackets at the vertical edges, and plank seam lines on the front face.

For planks and seams, I decide to just let the texture handle it—painting vertical boards with dark gap lines via canvas rather than modeling geometry, scaling proportionally per face. I'm setting up the rust-colored iron material and planning a canvas-based wood texture generator with varied board colors and grain noise, followed by a skull texture next.

Now I'm sketching the skull texture: drawing the cranium, jaw, eye sockets, nose, and teeth on canvas, with crossed bones behind it, all painted onto an opaque dark iron-brown background plaque material. I'm starting to write the actual code with a seeded RNG helper and a canvas texture generator function.

Writing texture helper functions...

Defining materials for each treasure chest element...

Adding vertical straps, decorative studs along the bands, and corner brackets to finish the chest's hardware details.

Now I'm working through the skull plaque placement with its iron frame and rivets, then adjusting positions of the hasp, straps, and hanging padlock so they don't overlap with the skull or each other.

Still detailing padlock...

Now I'm moving to the lid structure, building a pivoted group with a half-cylinder shell rotated and positioned so its flat base aligns correctly and its arc spans the right depth.

For the end caps, I'm constructing half-disc shapes using arc paths, then rotating and translating them so they sit flush at both ends of the cylindrical shell, matching up the local coordinate mapping carefully so the pieces align without gaps.

I'm now working out the lid straps using rotated torus arcs, orienting them along the barrel's X-axis so each ring forms a half-circle sitting slightly outside the shell radius, then placing studs along those arcs at evenly spaced angles to decorate the strap curve.

For the coins, I'm setting up an instanced mesh of flat cylinders scattered across a pile with randomized position, tilt, and rotation, using an elliptical mound function so coins sit higher toward the center and taper off toward the edges for a realistic heap shape.

I'm adding a spilled trail of coins lying flat on the floor in front of the chest, a looped pearl necklace draped over the coin pile using instanced spheres along a Catmull-Rom curve, and scattered ruby and emerald gems both on the pile and the floor.

For the goblet, I'm lathing a profile into a bowl-and-stem shape with a gem on the stem and a rim band of small gems, positioning it so it sinks slightly into the coin pile.

I'm adding iron feet and hinge knuckles to the chest body, then sketching out a canvas texture for a skull-and-crossbones plaque -- drawing the crossbones first, then layering the cranium, jaw, eye sockets, nose, and teeth on top.

Now I'm assembling all the materials (wood, iron, rust, brass, gold, pearl, ruby, emerald, dark accents, and the skull plaque texture) and writing the main build function that constructs the chest body, lid pivot with rotation, hinge straps, and the hanging padlock with its shackle threaded through a hasp ring.

Writing padlock shackle geometry...

I'm positioning the skull plaque centered on the front panel with corner bolt studs, making sure it doesn't collide with the horizontal iron bands or the hasp, then adding rows of decorative studs along the front and back bands while skipping the spots near the padlock and plaque to avoid overlap.

Writing the stud placement loops...

With all the pieces mapped out, I'm now writing the final assembled build function.
